_comment: THE STAGING RULINGS. This file is DATA, not code: flipping a ruling is an
edit here and no edit anywhere else, which is the whole point of it being
a manifest. oncotriage/staging/exclusions.py reads it, validates it, and
REFUSES on any defect -- item 11a's line, a configuration fault that one
edit fixes raises rather than degrading.
LAYERING, stated because it decides what a stale entry costs. The path
rules below are POLICY and PERFORMANCE: they record what an operator
decided and they stop the walk descending into 180 GB nobody wants. They
are NOT the secrets guarantee. The guarantee is the content-and-filename
scan in oncotriage/staging/secrets_scan.py, which runs over the SURVIVING
set on every invocation and refuses the whole run on a single hit. So a
path rule that goes stale under a rename degrades performance and record
keeping; it does not open a hole.
Paths are relative to the PROJECT ROOT (oncotriage.paths.main_path), use
forward slashes, are case-sensitive, and match on whole path components --
'02- Data/04- MeSH' does not match '02- Data/04- MeSHX'.

OPERATOR RULING CORRECTED HERE, and the correction is recorded rather than applied silently. The brief listed 'Fixture Backups' and 'The 42 Patients' as excluded and located them 'inside 03- Code'; they are at the PROJECT ROOT, in this directory, and 03- Code/09- Testing holds only the ragas venv. Excluding two children of a directory that is itself unstaged would be a no-op, and the two SURVIVING children are load-bearing: 'Characterization Fixtures' holds the twelve recordings that pin the Qdrant collection digest (the brief's own requirement 5 calls that pin the thing the snapshot makes recoverable) and 'Evaluation Runs' holds the paid evaluation campaign manifests. Both are 'data the campaign consumes' and 'results' under the brief's own staging rationale, so the parent is staged and the two ruled-disposable children are pruned below.

path_names_non_paths.name: _main_path_source
path_names_non_paths.reason: oncotriage.paths.PATH_NAMES has 20 members and this one is NOT a path -- it resolves to the string 'fallback' or 'environment', recording where the project root came from. It is declared here rather than skipped by a heuristic so that a future non-path member fails the cross-check instead of being silently classified as an unstaged directory.

secret_scan_allowlist.reason: A DELIBERATE TEST SENTINEL, NOT A CREDENTIAL. The file assigns a constant named _SENTINEL carrying an 'sk-' prefixed literal into OPENAI_API_KEY and then requires it to appear in no MLflow parameter key and no value -- the tracking pass's proof that a credential cannot reach the tracking store. The shape is genuine, so the scanner is RIGHT to flag it and must keep flagging that shape; this is the escape hatch rather than a detector change. THIS REASON DELIBERATELY DOES NOT QUOTE THE MATCHED VALUE, and the first draft did: quoting it made THIS MANIFEST credential-shaped, the next dry run flagged s3_staging_exclusions.json itself, and the fix would have been a second allowlist entry quoting the first. An allowlist that describes what it excuses stays out of its own scan. THE COST, STATED: the key includes the file's sha256, so any edit to that test expires the excuse and the next staging run refuses until a human re-reads the finding and re-allowlists. That is the intended direction -- an excuse that survived edits would be a permanent hole under a path somebody later reuses.
